children: GameStop Corp. (GME, Financials) just received a big endorsement from its own house. Director Lawrence Cheng purchased 55,000 shares through Cheng Capital LLC for around $1.03 million.
He paid an average $18.7992 per share, boosting Cheng Capital's declared stake to 143,000 shares. The buy is of a remarkable size. Timing makes it more fascinating.
Cheng bought the shares on the same day that GameStop published fiscal second-quarter results that beat analysts' expectations. Insider buying is not always a sign a stock is going up.
But investors do take heed when directors put their own money in, especially when they get a fresh look at the company's latest figures.

That's important as it pertains to GameStop, where investors are still debating about how much of its worth is in its basic retail operation and how much is based on the company's cash and future strategy.
Cheng's purchase doesn't answer those questions. It does suggest one director was willing to back the shares with more than $1 million at current levels.
The question now for investors is whether one good quarter is enough for GameStop to build something more sustainable.

title: GameStop Director Puts $1 Million Behind the Stock After Earnings
